reports.title: Machine Learning Methods to Predict Incidence Risk of Altitude Decompression Sickness
reports.reason: The public abstract identifies ADRAC computer output and prior published observations. Original operational chamber outcomes are unavailable in the abstract. Full paper pending access.

reports.title: Cardiac decompression sickness after hypobaric chamber training: case report of a coronary gas embolism.
reports.reason: Retain one cardiac dysbarism case, suspected coronary gas embolism. Clinical attribution and cohort denominator are unresolved.

reports.title: Incidence of decompression sickness in individuals tested in a decompression chamber situated at 4,700 feet.
reports.locator: pp. 279, 281 and 286, Methods and Tables I and VII
reports.reason: Purpose-defined qualification tests used repeated chamber exposures. The historical composite and run counts are contextual, with no separate routine-training group.

reports.title: Type II altitude decompression sickness (DCS): U.S. Air Force experience with 133 cases.
reports.locator: pp. 257-261, Methods, Results and Tables I-III
reports.reason: Retain treated chamber cases as descriptive treatment evidence. Chamber-specific occupation and at-risk exposure denominators are unavailable. Preserve possible overlap with Davis, Weien and related USAF series.

reports.title: Latent Presentation of Decompression Sickness After Altitude Chamber Training in an Active Duty Flier.
reports.reason: Retain delayed source-attributed post-training DCS as one case, with recurrence as a milestone. The Studer report concerns a different patient.

reports.title: A blitz of bends: decompression sickness in four students after hypobaric chamber training.
reports.locator: pp. 600-602, Case Histories, Figure 1 and Discussion
reports.reason: Retain the two preexisting HALO risk sets. Four cases are common to both margins. A helicopter flight preceded next-morning presentation. The standard Fort Rucker cohort excluded HALO.

reports.title: Low incidence of bends following renitrogenation in an altitude training profile.
reports.reason: Retain the source's severity-specific zero. All-grade bends is reported below 0.5% without an exact count. Profile attendance is recorded as subjects. Dates and overlap with Furry are unverified.

reports.title: Some Factors Affecting the Incidence of “Bends” At Altitude
reports.locator: Oxford article landing page and Yale finding aid p. 118
reports.reason: Public publisher metadata and Yale correspondence locator verified. Full text unavailable. Archive lead is box 272, folder 161, John Farquhar Fulton Papers.

reports.title: DECOMPRESSION SICKNESS: Some Factors Which Affect the Incidence of Bends at Altitude
reports.reason: Public preview ends before full methods and results. Study scope and possible overlap with the earlier radiographic report remain uncertain.

reports.title: Decompression Sickness Following Altitude-Chamber Training
reports.locator: pp. 11 and 14, Case Presentation and Conclusion
reports.reason: Retain one presumptive Type II DCS case after training. There is no exposed-cohort denominator. Preserve separate report and patient identity from Gentry.

reports.title: Incidence of bends pain in a short exposure to simulated altitudes of 26,000, 28,000 and 30,000 feet.
reports.reason: Controlled chamber exposures varied altitude, temperature and activity. The 1,731 experimental man-flights are outside the routine-training estimand.

reports.title: High-altitude decompression illness: case report and discussion.
reports.reason: Retain the sequential exposure DCI narrative. Three cases first appeared in commercial flight after chamber training. The course had 17 trainees. The number undertaking both exposures is unknown.

reports.title: Investigation of a cluster of decompression sickness cases following a high-altitude chamber flight.
